name: U.S. Virgin Islands
summary: The U.S. Virgin Islands have no forced heirship for children in the sources found, and Title 15 follows Uniform Probate Code ideas. Common-law trusts apply. No private foundation law was found and the Hague Trusts Convention is not in force for the United States.
family_claims: Title 15 of the Virgin Islands Code follows the Uniform Probate Code. Whether it gives a surviving spouse an elective share was not verified.
foreign_law_note: No source read states the Virgin Islands' conflict rule for a foreign national's estate.
trust_note: HCCH shows the United States as signatory only, with no extension. Fiduciary relations sit in Title 15, chs. 51-65. No private foundation statute was found.
open_questions: Elective share and family allowance rules not read.
Title 15 text was seen only as a table of contents.
Trust and foundation statutes not verified.
Private foundations: no source found either way; not finding a foundation law is not evidence that there is none.
